title: FraudCoins open dataset: on-chain holder concentration and contract permissions
description:
On-chain holder-concentration measurements and contract-permission data for cryptocurrency tokens, published as plain JSON under CC BY 4.0.

A raw "top 10 holders hold X%" figure counts whatever the ten largest addresses happen to be — routinely an exchange's omnibus wallet, a liquidity pool, a bridge contract, a locked treasury or a burn address. This dataset classifies each of the ten largest holders first, publishes the share held by private wallets only, and names each wallet set aside with its classification and stake, so the correction can be verified on a block explorer rather than taken on trust.

Reading it correctly: null means no measurement, never a clean result. A flat interval in the history series means no observed change, not a daily re-measurement. Flag thresholds are per tier (50% above 50 million USD market cap, 70% for the rotated 10–50 million USD tier) and require at least 50 holder records.

Limitations: holder classification relies on public address labels, so an unlabelled custodial wallet is counted as private and every correction is a floor rather than a complete accounting. Excluded supply is not automatically harmless — treasury and vesting holdings can reach the market on unlock. Contract data comes from third-party static analysis of the deployed contract; trade-simulation verdicts (honeypot, cannot-sell-all, taxes) are deliberately excluded because they produce false positives on legitimate, freely-traded assets. Risk scores and flags are automated, opinion-based assessments derived from public market data — not statements of fact, financial advice, or allegations of illegal conduct against any project or person.
